newsitem.title: USA: Alex. Brown, BT deal called snag-free--arbs.
newsitem.headline: Alex. Brown, BT deal called snag-free--arbs.

text.p: Alex. Brown Inc stock raced to the head of the New York Stock Exchange percent-gainers list Monday as investors backed the firm's $1.7 billion merger with Bankers Trust New York Corp, arbitrageurs said.

"I see no fine print in the deal. It is relatively issue-free and the shares are trading extremely tightly to reflect that," said an arbitrageur, referring to the relatively small difference between the market prices of the shares and the terms in the agreement.
In morning trade, Alex. Brown shares were up 10-7/8, or 20.5 percent, to 64 in unusually vigorous dealings.
Earlier this morning, Alex. Brown shares reached a high of 64-3/8, eclipsing the old year-high of 64 reached February 19.

Monday's gain built on a significant run-up in the shares Friday, when Alex. Brown stock climbed 8-1/2 points, or 19 percent, as the market speculated about a merger involving the Baltimore-based investment bank.
"There was a lot of interest in Alex. Brown. It is a crown jewel and everyone wanted to own it. The (Banker Trust) deal seems pretty straightforward," added a second arbitrageur.
Meanwhile, Bankers Trust shares were off 1-7/8 to 80-3/8 on the NYSE.
According to the terms of the deal, announced late Sunday night, each Alex. Brown common share would be exchanged for 0.83 share of Bankers Trust.
"It is the way of the future because of the breaking down of Glass-Steagall and the need for banks to generate more fee income and to become less interest-rate sensitive," said the first arbitrageur.

Glass-Steagall refers to a 1933 law separating commercial banking and investment banking, though regulators have recently raised the limitation on how much securities underwriting a bank can do through a securities affiliate.
The arbs and other traders said the deal has reignited takeover speculation among brokerage stocks.

Indeed, just behind Alex Brown on the NYSE percent-gainers list was Piper Jaffray Cos, up 1-7/8, or 12.7 percent, to 16-5/8, followed by Raymond James Financial Inc, up 2-5/8, or 12.7 percent, to 23-3/8.
